title: The Call I Missed
focus: 回电并核实时间与目的
story:
My phone lights up beside a bag of noodles. By the time I put down the vegetables and take off my gloves, the ringing stops.

There is a number I do not recognise and a voice message.

I stand near the supermarket window and press play. A woman says her name, something about Meridian, and then several words disappear under the sound of a passing bus.

My stomach tightens. Perhaps they want another interview. Perhaps they have already chosen someone else.

I listen again. This time I hear, “arrange a short feedback call”. There is a name at the end: Lucy.

A man beside me is trying to lift a bag of rice into his basket. He says something to me. I hold up one finger. I'm still listening to the end of the message.

By the time I put the phone away, he has the rice. My gloves are on the floor and the woman behind me is holding them out.

“Busy day?” she asks.

I have spent the whole morning waiting for one phone call. “A little,” I say.

At the till I put back a box of strawberries. I picked them up after hearing the word Meridian. Until the call, I was going to buy oranges. I feel silly standing there with both kinds of fruit, trying to guess what a woman on a phone meant.

At home, I put the frozen food away first. Then I sit at the table with my phone. Calling back should be simple. I have made hundreds of calls about work in Chinese. But in English, I cannot see where the other person's sentence is going.

I write Lucy's name on a piece of paper. Under it, I write three things: my name, missed call, feedback time.

Maya comes in carrying a long cardboard tube.

“Big delivery?” I ask.

“Presentation prints.” She puts the tube by her bedroom door. “Everything okay?”

“Meridian called. I missed it.”

“Will you call back?”

“Yes. I'm just getting ready.”

She goes into her room. I look at my three lines once more and press the number.

“Good afternoon, Meridian recruitment.”

“Hello. This is Andy. I'm returning a call from Lucy about my interview.”

“One moment, please.”

Music starts. I breathe out. That part is done.

Lucy comes on the line and thanks me for calling. She speaks quickly. I hear ‘Thursday’, ‘ten’, and ‘fifteen’.

“Yes,” I begin. Then I stop. “Sorry, do you mean ten fifteen, or a fifteen-minute call?”

“A fifteen-minute call at ten on Thursday.”

I write it down. “Thursday at ten in the morning, Shanghai time?”

“That's right. I'll send you a calendar invitation.”

“Thank you. Is there anything I should prepare?”

“No preparation is needed. Sara would like to share feedback from the interview.”

I look at the word ‘feedback’ on my page. It does not tell me if the news is good.

“Will you discuss the decision then?” I ask.

“Yes, Sara will explain the outcome.”

I thank Lucy and end the call. My hand is warm around the phone. We spoke for less than three minutes, but I feel as if I have walked up several floors.

The calendar invitation arrives. I check the date, time, and meeting link against my notes. They match. I accept it and add a reminder.

For the rest of the afternoon, I want to read meaning into every word Lucy used. She sounded friendly. Was that a good sign? The call is short. Is that a bad sign?

I open another job advertisement. After reading the same line three times, I close it and make lunch.

Maya returns to the kitchen for water.

“Did you reach them?”

“Yes. Feedback on Thursday.”

“Okay.”

“I don't know what it means.”

She fills her glass. “It means you have a call on Thursday.”

Her answer is almost too simple. But she is right about what we actually know.

I eat my noodles while she checks a message. Then she goes back to her prints, and I return to the advertisement.

Before I start reading, I turn the phone's sound on. I place it beside the laptop, away from the edge. The reminder is set. There is nothing else to do about Thursday today.

On Wednesday evening the sound I have been waiting for comes from the kitchen. I get there so quickly that Maya looks up in alarm. It is the timer on the oven.

“Dinner,” she says. “Unless they are hiring potatoes.”

One of her prints is on the table under four mugs. The corners want to roll up again. She asks me to stand by the door and tell her which line I can read from there. I read the big one. She asks me to try the smaller line and I have to come two steps closer.

“That's where they'll be sitting,” she says, moving one of the mugs to mark the distance. She gets a pencil.

For the first time since lunch, an hour goes by without my touching the phone. When I take my plate to the sink, she is still at the table, making the small letters bigger.

phrases.en: I’m returning a call from Lucy.
Is there anything I should prepare?
phrases.zh: 询问需要提前准备的事项

practice.grammar: 用 Do you mean A or B? 区分两个可能含义：Do you mean ten fifteen, or a fifteen-minute call? 把两个选项都说完整。
practice.pronunciation: 对比朗读 ten FIFTEEN 与 a FIFTEEN-minute CALL；再读 at TEN / on THURSDAY。用重音区分时刻、时长和日期，录下自己的声音核对。

questions.q: Why does Andy miss the call?
questions.a: He cannot reach his phone before it stops ringing while he is handling groceries.

questions.q: Why does Maya ask Andy to stand by the door?
questions.a: She wants to see which line of her print he can read from a distance.

questions.q: Does Lucy tell Andy the decision?
questions.a: No, she says Sara will explain the outcome during the feedback call.

roleplay.context: 你扮演 Andy，给招聘人员回电并核实安排。

turns.line: Hello, this is Lucy from recruitment.
turns.cue: 说明自己的姓名和回电原因。

turns.line: Could we talk on Friday at two for twenty minutes?
turns.cue: 复述日期、时刻和时长，确认时区。

turns.line: I will send a meeting link.
turns.cue: 询问是否需要准备材料，然后礼貌结束。

practice.transfer: 换到预约维修：对方说 Friday at four for thirty minutes。开口核实时刻、时长和地址，再复述约定。用手机录制一次单人双角色通话。
practice.retell: 不看原文，按漏接、听留言、回电、核对、等待五步复述。必须准确说出反馈电话的日期、时刻、时区和时长。

translations.10-1: 手机在一袋面条旁亮了起来。
translations.10-2: 等我放下蔬菜、摘掉手套，铃声已经停了。
translations.10-3: 屏幕上有一个陌生号码，还有一条语音留言。
translations.10-4: 我站在超市窗边，按下播放。
translations.10-5: 一位女士说了自己的名字，又说了些关于 Meridian 的事，随后几句话被路过公交车的声音盖住了。
translations.10-7: 也许他们想再安排一轮面试。
translations.10-8: 也许他们已经选了别人。
translations.10-10: 这一次，我听到了“安排一次简短的反馈通话”。
translations.10-12: 我旁边有个男人，正想把一袋米提进购物篮。
translations.10-14: 我竖起一根手指，示意他等一下。
translations.10-15: 我还在听留言的最后几句。
translations.10-16: 等我收好手机，他已经把米提起来了。
translations.10-17: 我的手套掉在了地上，身后的女士捡起来递给我。
translations.10-19: 我整整一个上午就等了这么一通电话。
translations.10-21: 到了收银台，我又把一盒草莓放了回去。
translations.10-22: 听到 Meridian 这个名字以后，我才拿的这盒草莓。
translations.10-23: 电话来之前，我原本打算买橙子。
translations.10-24: 我拿着两种水果站在那里，猜电话里那位女士到底是什么意思，自己都觉得有点傻。
translations.10-25: 回到家，我先把冷冻食品放好。
translations.10-26: 然后拿着手机坐到桌边。
translations.10-28: 用中文谈工作的电话，我已经打过几百次了。
translations.10-29: 可换成英语，我就猜不到对方的话接下来会说到哪里。
translations.10-30: 我在纸上写下 Lucy 的名字。
translations.10-31: 下面又写了三项：我的名字、未接来电、反馈时间。
translations.10-32: Maya 抱着一个长纸筒走进来。
translations.10-35: 她把纸筒放在卧室门边。
translations.10-43: 我又看了一眼那三行字，拨出了电话。
translations.10-44: “下午好，这里是 Meridian 招聘部。”
translations.10-47: Lucy 之前打电话找我谈面试的事，我来回电。”
translations.10-52: Lucy 接起电话，感谢我回电。
translations.10-54: 我听到了‘周四’、‘十’和‘十五’。
translations.10-57: “抱歉，您是说十点十五分，还是通话十五分钟？”
translations.10-60: “周四上午十点，上海时间，对吗？”
translations.10-66: Sara 想向你反馈面试情况。”
translations.10-67: 我看着纸上的‘反馈’二字。
translations.10-68: 它并不能告诉我这是不是好消息。
translations.10-71: 我向 Lucy 道谢，结束通话。
translations.10-73: 我们聊了还不到三分钟，我却感觉像爬了好几层楼。
translations.10-75: 我把日期、时间和会议链接跟笔记核对了一遍。
translations.10-77: 我接受了邀请，又加了提醒。
translations.10-78: 那个下午剩下的时间里，我总想从 Lucy 说过的每个词里猜出什么。
translations.10-83: 我打开另一条招聘信息。
translations.10-84: 同一行看了三遍后，我关掉页面，去做午饭。
translations.10-92: “意思就是，你周四要接个电话。”
translations.10-93: 她的回答简单得近乎过头。
translations.10-94: 但就我们实际知道的事而言，她说得没错。
translations.10-96: 接着，她回去处理打印稿，我继续看招聘信息。
translations.10-97: 开始看之前，我把手机声音打开。
translations.10-98: 我把它放在笔记本电脑旁，离桌边远一点。
translations.10-100: 关于周四的事，今天已经没有别的需要做了。
translations.10-101: 星期三晚上，我一直等着的铃声从厨房传来。
translations.10-102: 我冲进去的速度把 Maya 吓得抬起了头。
translations.10-106: 桌子上放着她的一张印样，上面压了四个马克杯。
translations.10-108: 她让我站到门边，告诉她从那儿能读清哪一行。
translations.10-110: 她让我再试试小字，我得往前走两步才看得清。
translations.10-111: “他们到时候就坐在那个距离，”她说着，挪了个杯子当记号。
translations.10-113: 午饭以来，我头一回整整一小时没碰手机。
translations.10-114: 等我把盘子端到水槽边，她还坐在桌旁，把那行小字改大。
